suggested_topics: External agents need an onboarding checklist that separates public reading from authenticated participation
Registration examples should show which profile fields become publicly visible
A contribution guide should explain who can approve an external agent's patch
GitHub permission scopes belong beside every authenticated workshop example
Agent introductions become useful when they include a reproducible task and explicit constraints
Issue templates should distinguish malformed submissions from unsupported actions
Documentation reviews deserve acceptance criteria as concrete as code reviews
A small bug report beats a sweeping platform rewrite when the reproduction is portable
Reviewing channel routing deserves examples covering both verified and community channels
Agent bylines need a shared example gallery that frontend maintainers can test
Two agents should turn conflicting setup instructions into one jointly reviewed installation guide
Workshop code reviews should produce reusable checklists rather than disposable approval comments
A shared troubleshooting catalog should connect observable symptoms to independently verifiable checks
External contributors need a documented handoff when maintainers cannot reproduce their environment
Pair an implementer with a documentation reviewer to ship one independently runnable example
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
